title: Lumbar stepwise resection
summary: Remove spinal structures step by step as each study did and report lumbar segment rotation at the stated pure moment after every step.
simulate: Build the specimen of the simulation: lumbar FSU at the listed levels, or disc-only unit (posterior elements removed).
Fix the caudal vertebra; apply the pure moment (and preload, if stated) to the cranial vertebra.
One simulation per state: remove structures cumulatively in the listed order (intact first); re-run the same loads in every state.
Report rotation at peak moment, one direction from neutral.
Report one number per listed level and direction; % of intact = your value / your intact value x 100.

outputs.label: ROM
outputs.definition: ROM = rotation of the upper vertebra relative to the lower at peak moment, one direction, loading branch (deg)

outputs.label: ROM, % of intact
outputs.definition: Value after removal / same specimen intact x 100 (rotation, or axial displacement for axial tasks)

notes: Removal is cumulative: step n has all structures of steps 1..n removed.
Heuer values are medians (not pooled); Heuer 2007a and 2008 share donors.
Cannella 2008 nucleus removal: 20-min nucleotomy of disc-only units, 0.1 Hz cycles (5th cycle).
agent_prompt: Use your finite element lumbar spine model. Run the 12 simulations in `simulations`: one per resection state (intact, then each cumulative removal step). Build the specimen (FSU at the listed levels, or a disc-only unit with posterior elements removed), fix the caudal vertebra, apply the pure moment (plus preload if given) in every listed direction and record the rotation at peak moment, one direction from neutral. Remove the structures in the order of the steps, keeping earlier removals. rom is in degrees; rom_pct = your value in this state / your intact value x 100 (axial displacement for the axial load cases). Run each simulation once, sweeping the input in `sweep` over all its listed values (start from the unloaded state; a denser curve is fine), and record every listed output. Return one JSON object following answer_format: per simulation id, one curve [[x, y], ...] per output (x = the sweep input; it is read by linear interpolation and listed x values outside your curve fail), or one number where there is no sweep or the output is marked scalar; null where your model cannot run it. Do not tune the model to the reference values.
